summary: I chaired the first internal HEP weekly progress meeting in Tashkent and recorded the actions on the transformer specification, the APG/Performance Security bank evidence and the medical evacuation route. I issued the Progress Measurement and Reporting Procedure (Rev A) for review and updated A020 to 100%, A030 to 50% and A040 to 33%. Rain caused a partial stoppage at site, so no site progress was measured today.

sections.heading: 1. Purpose and Scope
paragraphs: This procedure defines how Helios EPC LLC (HEP) measures, weights, certifies and reports progress on the HELIOS 100 MW PV + BESS Power Plant (HEL001). It applies to engineering, procurement, construction, testing and commissioning, and to the subcontractors Navoi Qurilish, SteelPro Montaj, UzElectroMontaj and GridWorks Central Asia, and to the vendors SunPeak, VoltEdge, AxisTrack and CellCore. It is the single basis for the monthly progress report, the weekly look-ahead, the one-page dashboard and the S-curve submitted to QSE and Meridian, and it supports payment milestones and any extension of time analysis under the Contract.

The procedure is issued as Rev A for review by the Project Director and will be reflected in PEP Rev A (reporting and communication section). Comments are requested by 11 December 2026 so that the first monthly report (December 2026, due 5 January 2027) is produced under the final rules.

sections.heading: 3. Progress Measurement Principles
paragraphs: Progress is measured against the approved baseline schedule (Level 1-3, A040) using a single physical percent-complete per activity. Progress is based on objective evidence only: approved deliverables, signed delivery notes, measured installed quantities and signed inspection records. Opinion-based percentages are not accepted, and no activity is reported above 90% until its closing evidence is on file.

Every activity carries one measurement method (Section 4). Activity logic is not altered when progress is updated; any change to logic, durations or constraints is recorded as a schedule revision with a reason. Actual start and finish dates are those evidenced by the site diary, transmittals or delivery records.

sections.heading: 4. Weighting and Earned-Value Rules by Discipline
paragraphs: Weights are proposed here pending cost loading of the baseline. Project weights will be fixed when the baseline is approved and then frozen, except through approved changes. Within each discipline, activity weight is proportional to budgeted manhours or contract value.

rows: Level of effort, spread evenly over the contract duration
Per deliverable: 20% started, 50% issued for review, 80% approved by OWE (Code A/B), 100% IFC issued; weighted by manhours
Per package: 10% RFQ issued, 25% award/PO, 40% design/vendor documents approved, 70% FAT passed and shipped, 90% delivered to site, 100% inspected and accepted
Measured quantities: piles driven, foundations poured, trenches and roads completed, accepted with signed ITP
Installed units against total (piles to module mounting), earned only after QC acceptance
Installed cable metres, terminated strings, installed inverter stations, with QC records
Milestone-based per stage: foundations, steel erection, equipment installed, stringing, testing
Per test procedure completed and certificate signed: pre-commissioning, energisation, performance test, PAC

sections.heading: 5. Progress Cut-off and Data Collection
bullets: Weekly cut-off: Saturday 24:00 (site works Monday to Saturday); data to Planning by Monday 12:00.
Weekly progress meeting: Thursday, internal HEP meeting first, then the Client weekly meeting as agreed at the Kick-off Meeting.
Monthly cut-off: last calendar day of each month. Report issued to QSE and Meridian by the 5th of the following month. First report covers December 2026 and is due 5 January 2027.
Subcontractors submit weekly progress by Monday 10:00 on the HEP template, with quantities, manpower and equipment.
Progress claimed after cut-off is carried to the next period. Late data is flagged in the report and not backdated.
The Planning Engineer reviews the submitted progress, checks it against the Construction Manager and QA/QC records, and records any difference in the update log.

sections.heading: 6. Schedule Update and Delay Recording
paragraphs: After each cut-off the schedule is statused in Primavera P6 with actual dates, physical percent complete and remaining durations. The updated schedule is compared with the baseline, and the critical path and near-critical paths (float below 15 days) are reported. Variance of more than 5 days on any critical activity or more than 10 days on any other Level 2 milestone requires a written recovery proposal from the activity owner within 2 working days.

Every delay event is logged in the delay register with date, cause, affected activities, responsible party and contemporaneous record. The register is the source for any time impact analysis and for notices under the Contract, prepared with Thomas Becker. Weather stoppage, such as rain and sub-zero days, is recorded day by day with site diary reference.

sections.heading: 8. S-curve, Earned Value Indicators and Forecast
paragraphs: The S-curve is built from the baseline weighted progress, resource-loaded once the baseline is approved. Until then, a time-phased profile based on the Level 2 milestone schedule is used and labelled as provisional. From the first report after approval, schedule performance index (SPI = earned / planned) and forecast completion date are reported. Cost indicators (CPI) are produced with Thomas Becker for internal use only, unless the Contract requires otherwise.
The Project Director's weekly critical items, the 220/33 kV transformer (R-001) and the geotechnical/Basic Design negative float (R-003), are shown on every dashboard with owner, mitigation and date.

sections.heading: 9. Review, Records and Revision
paragraphs: This procedure is reviewed after the first monthly report and after baseline approval. Records (weekly progress sheets, update logs, reports) are filed under 1_Project_Mgmt/07_Communications and 1_Project_Mgmt/04_Schedule by the Document Controller. Revisions are numbered per the Document Control and Numbering Procedure.

emails.subject: Progress Measurement Procedure Rev A and Weekly Meeting No. 1 actions
emails.body:
Rajan,

The first internal weekly meeting is minuted and the actions are issued with owners and dates. The Progress Measurement and Reporting Procedure Rev A is issued for your review. Proposed discipline weights (engineering 8%, procurement 52%, construction 32%) are provisional until the baseline is cost loaded. I am closing PEP comments 1-7 by 11 December and will send the revised PEP, the Level 1 summary and the reporting calendar by 10 December as requested.

I note that A040 stands at 33% and the first L2 draft is still due 21 December. The baseline input actions ACTIONS-000-006 and ACTIONS-000-007 are still open and will move that date if not received by Friday.

Aziz Karimov

items.discussion: Aziz Karimov opened the first internal HEP weekly meeting at the Tashkent office. Rajan Iyer set the rule that the meeting is held on Thursdays after this first Tuesday session, with the internal meeting held before the Client weekly meeting. Actions from the Kick-off Meeting were reviewed and the status below was accepted.

items.topic: Schedule status A020, A030, A040, A050, A710
items.discussion: A020 Kick-off and team mobilisation is closed at 100% following this meeting. A030 PEP and procedures stands at 50%: PEP Rev A is approved for internal issue by the Project Director, subject to comments 1-7. A040 baseline L1-L3 is at 33%: L1/L2 are issued for review and L3 is being built, with the first L2 draft due 21 December and submission for approval by 10 January 2027. A050 stands at 6%: forms are with QSE. A710 subcontracting strategy and prequalification is at 10%. Aziz Karimov noted that rain today stopped part of the site works, with no impact on these activities.

Rajan Iyer's seven comments were walked through. Aziz Karimov will close them in the same revision by 11 December, including the exact KOM reporting format, review periods with deemed-approval wording marked as to be confirmed by Thomas Becker, the R-001 and R-003 critical items with mitigation owners and dates, and the M05 versus M07 controlled assumption. Arun Pillai's quality points (QMP comments due 21 December, hold points, vendor FATs, audits before 1 March 2027) are to be included.

Inputs due today were reviewed. Planning confirmed that the baseline cannot move to L3 without durations and logic from Engineering (design package timing) and Construction (productivity and mobilisation sequence). Elena Petrova will provide the design document register and construction permit file timing; Sanjay Mehta will provide productivity assumptions and the sequence for M05 to M08. Any item still missing on 11 December will be shown in the baseline as an assumption.

Rajan Iyer repeated that 18 December is a hold date and not a target. Elena Petrova is to confirm by 9 December that the date is secure and name the author, with the assumptions and ranges for values depending on the Basic Design and UzGridCo. Mehmet Yıldız needs the specification for RFQ on 4 January 2027 and award on 12 February 2027. Early Meridian review is to run in parallel. Planning will show the item as R-001 (score 20) on the dashboard.

items.topic: APG and Performance Security bank evidence
items.discussion: Thomas Becker reported that QSE comments on the forms were received on 7 December and QSE response on the issuing bank is due 9 December. HEP must provide bank rating evidence and the signatory specimen sheet. The target for agreed forms is 11 December, and delay would put the advance payment (M03, 5 January 2027) and NTP preconditions at risk. Thomas Becker will obtain written confirmation of the bank's rating evidence and report on 10 December.

items.topic: HSE early-access requirements and medical evacuation
items.discussion: Jamshid Tursunov presented the early-access requirements for the survey and geotechnical crews from 20 December: induction, PPE, site emergency plan, communications and first aid. The medical evacuation route from site to the nearest hospital in Navoi (12 km unpaved track to A-380, then onward) is not yet confirmed in writing; he will confirm it with the hospital and Sanjay Mehta. Winter conditions with rain and temperatures of -3 to 6 degrees C are included in the plan.

Aziz Karimov presented the procedure issued today: weighting by discipline, earned-value rules, weekly cut-off Saturday, monthly cut-off on the last day of the month with issue by the 5th, weekly look-ahead, one-page dashboard and S-curve. The proposed weights are provisional until the baseline is cost loaded. Disciplines are to return comments by 11 December. Arun Pillai confirmed that progress will only be earned with signed QC records.

items.topic: Look-ahead to NTP on 15 December and to the Client weekly meeting on 10 December
items.discussion: Items to be ready for NTP: approved APG and Performance Security forms, insurance evidence, PEP Rev A, first design document register and baseline process. For the Client weekly meeting on 10 December, the team agreed the position on land allocation (A110, QSE letter due 10 December), PEP issue date 15 December and first L2 draft date 21 December. The next internal meeting is on Thursday 10 December before the Client meeting. Meeting closed.
